utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: My client wants to address to the Court and to say that the Lions unit was not formed by him. It was formed by Macedonian government. It's legal -- in a legal and proper way. And they were also disband after the end of the crisis in a proper and legal way. That was just what he was trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. If your client feels that he needs to add something over and above what you have said, then he's free to do so. Usually the practice is you speak on his behalf, but if -- I want to make it clear that if he wants to add anything, he's -- you are free to consult with him, he is free to consult with you, and if he wants the floor, we will give him the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. He would like to say something briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. GODZO
utterances.text: Whenever you -- we allow him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Boskoski, we are not forcing you to say anything. You have a right to remain silent during all these proceedings, but if you wish to say something, we will give you the floor. And I also wish to make it clear that since you have got this right of silence, if you decide to say something, whatever you say will be put on record and, if necessary, will be used later on in the proceedings. So it's up to you whether to proceed or not. THE ACCUSED BOSKOSKI: [Interpretation] Distinguished President, I did not have any intention to speak, Your Honour, but several -- several issues raised here have forced me to speak a bit and reiterate once again that the only minister of interior who since 2001, since the beginning of the conflict and the crisis in the Republic of Macedonia, has publicly through the Macedonian media and in cooperation with The Hague Tribunal confirmed that fully believes this high legal institution, the participants of which are we as well, the small but significant and important to the Republic of Macedonia, and the Republic of Macedonia being a member of the United Nations, at no moment has Ljube Boskoski as a politician, as a person, as a father of three minor children, and primarily as a person very fond of Republic of Macedonia and very fond of state of law, legal institutions, at no moment has he thought that his credibility, the credibility of his state, of its Euro-Atlantic orientations, of its reform processes are put into question by the fact of him leaving the Republic of Macedonia or, God forbid, flee from the Republic of Macedonia. I believe highly in this Court. I also believe in the Republic of Macedonia. I believe in the justice system. I am a legalist, and -- or a lawyer, and nobody can make me believe the opposite. Your Honour, there are different truths there but there aren't -- there is one universal truth and that God exists, and I believe in God. I believe that He is on my side, not since I'm Ljube Boskoski but because I speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am informed that we need a technical break. I think we have only got a few minutes left before we rise, but I understand that the technical break is needed now. Am I right? Yes. So how much time? All right. It's just changing of tapes, I suppose. All right. We'll wait. The sitting is suspended now, and I think we can all remain here, and when we are informed that the tapes are changed, then we can proceed and conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I'm informed that we can continue. I can assure everyone that this sitting will be over in a few minutes. That's -- and then we can conclude. So, yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, I would like to reply to the presentation by the distinguished Prosecutor. In the evidence that the Prosecutor's office has submitted to me regarding the indictment, there are statements by the accused Johan Tarculovski. So from it can be seen that at any invitation by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia that has informed him by a summons to appear for a hearing or an interview, Mr. Tarculovski has responded. But information received through other persons, these are inadmissible and illegal ways pursuant to the legislation of the Republic of Macedonia. The only way in which a person can be summoned is by a written summons which can be duly received personally by the accused or the indicted. This is the only reply I would like to give to the Prosecutor. With regards to the committee supporters of a football club, the Court informed us that they have been the organisers of the demonstrations on the 22nd of March. I wish to indicate for Court's attention that the accused Tarculovski, after he has been employed in 1999 in the security of the President Boris Trajkovska, has never appeared at a football match and let alone be a leader of this group. So with this respect I can inform the Court that he is neither leader nor he couldn't -- could have been the organiser of that group of football supporters. So I beg the Court to take these facts into account. This is a family man who has established a family, has a child, who possibly in his youth did go to football matches but this cannot be considered as a sin of his. Thank you. And I would like to inform the Court that Mr. Johan would like to address with two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tarculovski. The same advice that I gave the other co-accused: You have a right to remain silent. No one can force you to say anything in this Tribunal, but if you do speak, you do say something, then whatever you say may actually be used in evidence in due course. THE ACCUSED TARCULOVSKI: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are discussing today my application for provisional release which was filed on my behalf by my legal counsel. Everything that my counsel said I can only approve but also add a few sentences to it. Even though I have arrested and detained in prison, I assure you if I had only knew that there is an indictment against me, I would appear before the Courts -- before this Court myself. The same as I would have done it at that time, I am prepared to appear before the Court any time if I am -- if I am addressed. This Court is my only hope to prove my innocence and to return to my family; my daughter and my wife and my mother. My goal, my purpose is to take care of my family in freedom and prepare better my Defence. I thank you for listening to me and I hope you will have understanding to provisionally release me to be with my family in my home country of Macedonia. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Tarculovski. Prosecution, with regard to these incidents, demonstrations in March of this year, do you have any comments? Are they of concern to you or are they less serious in your mind than I may have presented them?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution thinks that they are serious in the sense that both accused do have a fanatical sort of support element following them in Macedonia. It doesn't -- it's not necessarily large. But by the nature of some of these members of the ex-Lions at the demonstration, calling for weapons, et cetera, that is a concern, especially in relation to witness intimidation, that sort of behaviour by people that associate themselves with the accused. Whether that's -- whether that can be seen to be the fault of the accused, that may not be the point, but the fact that it is occurring is a concern in relation to witness protection. But, Your Honours, as far as the accuracy of the information, which was the Confidential and Ex Parte Annex A to the 22nd of April, 2005, motion of the Prosecution, the Prosecution submits it's highly accurate. It initially was instigated by a number name of newspaper reports reporting these events. So as not just to put newspaper accounts of events, a particular mission was conducted in Macedonia and the two most significant security organisations down there were spoken to at length to get a full account, and I think you'll see from the annexes and the attachments that it's very comprehensive and very complete, and if anything further is required, Your Honour, we can call witnesses to that effect. As far as the interviews with Mr. Tarculovski, yes, he did give interviews in 2003, one when he was a member of the Ministry of Interior and one shortly afterwards. The circumstances in which he cooperated back then are quite different to the circumstances in which we say that he didn't cooperate recently. And just lastly, in relation to the tendering of exhibits, I would ask, unless there's an objection, that the bundle of items tagged 1 to 8 be tendered, even though we largely referred to tab 6, and they be tendered as P1. And I would also ask that the request for assistance with the Macedonian government in relation to attempts to locate and contact Mr. Tarculovski is headed RFA: BS/T07/MAC-0075, that be tendered as P2. And I would further ask that the attachments to the motions that have been put forward by the Prosecution also be tendered and by their virtue of attachment to the motion, and the Prosecution has no objections to the tendering of Defence exhibits in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. One final question to the Honourable Minister. We heard before that in Macedonia there is now -- either it exists already or it's in the making, a law on the protection of witnesses. Is it already in existence or is it in draft form, being debated in Parliament?

utterances.speaker: MS. MLADENOVSKA-GJORGJIVESKA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The law on protection of witnesses was passed in the Parliament in May. It is effective, but its implementation will start from January 1, 2006, due to taking additional activities needed to initiate its implementation. In the Ministry for the Interior, there is a department that should work in this matter, witness protection, and in the future period a council is to be -- witness protection council will be formed, and the law stipulates who will be the members of this council ex officio and also those who should be representatives of the certain bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Excellency, and I think it would be appreciated very much by this Trial Chamber if we obtain a copy of the relative legislation in your language, which we can then have translated. Yes. Is there any further business that the parties would like to transact? None? I see none. So the sitting is adjourned. We will hand down a written decision in due course, within a very short time. Thank you. I thank you, Excellency.
